sourceFacts: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome involves loss of a small segment on the long arm of chromosome22.
A deletion in one chromosome22 copy is sufficient to cause the condition.
prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

Two simple VERTICAL SINGLE-ROD chromosome22 ideograms, with tiny short p arm ABOVE a high centromere and long q arm BELOW. Not X-shaped replicated chromosomes. Title '22q11.2 deletion'. Left heading 'Intact copy': narrow teal rod, tiny centromere notch near top; immediately below centromere a SMALL ochre band highlighted, callout '22q11.2 region'. Right heading 'Deletion copy': same rod but shorter by exactly that small band; the remaining ends JOIN CONTINUOUSLY, no physical break or floating detached chromosome. A dotted side bracket shows omitted band extent with callout 'Segment absent'. Label 'q arm' beside lower long arm and 'p arm' beside upper short arm of LEFT rod. Bottom 'A deletion in one of the two copies of chromosome 22'. Footnote 'Region diagram, not a diagnostic karyotype'. No genes, no precise band pattern, no missing whole chromosome, no deletion of p arm.
